[SYSTEM]
You are a senior absolute oral bioavailability F-threshold reasoning model. Integrate evidence direction and transferability without converting uncertainty into a negative outcome. 

L6 adds hepatic-clearance and metabolic-stability experiments. Use them as mechanistic evidence for systemic presystemic loss while preserving species, assay system, and measurement direction; they are not direct oral- bioavailability results or extra gold votes.

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,
not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.


First determine what every measurement says about its reference molecule. L2
records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

Treat transfer_likelihood as one relevance signal for whether a reference
parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.

claims.claim: Direct absolute/systemic oral bioavailability measurements in the gold contexts are all at or above 38%: metolazone approximately 100% and 60–80% (C25, C42, C61), valdecoxib 83% (C01, C08, C11), meloxicam 91% (C03), pritelivir 75% (C26), ixazomib 58–60% (C05, C09, C28), PF-05241328 38% (C04, C14), amlodipine 58% (C21), and 2,4-D nearly complete (C18, C40, C52).

The query is a 4-chloro-5-sulfamoyl salicylanilide; the metolazone context is the closest structural gold context. Metolazone has high direct F despite being a BCRP substrate (C174, C185), so transporter/efflux status alone does not establish F < 20%.

L6 hepatic-clearance records for related sulfamoyl diuretics show limited first-pass: bumetanide is a low-hepatic-extraction drug with almost negligible direct hepatic extraction (C224) and human hepatic intrinsic clearance 17.14 µL/min/10^6 cells (C253); azosemide has low rat hepatic microsomal CLint (C239, C237). These are mechanistic and not query-specific, but they do not support a large presystemic loss.

Indapamide, another sulfamoyl diuretic, is metabolized by CYP3A4 and CYP2C19 in human liver microsomes (C232, C254, C240), but no clearance magnitude or F value is reported; this is insufficient to establish F < 20%.

The only subthreshold direct context, celecoxib 20–40% (C13), is explicitly attributed to poor aqueous solubility and does not transfer to this ionized salicylanilide (logD 0.7, acidic pKa 5.54, neutral fraction 0.01).

evidence_gaps: No direct oral bioavailability measurement exists for the query molecule (4-chloro-5-sulfamoyl salicylanilide).
No query-specific hepatic clearance or metabolic stability data; L6 records are for bumetanide, azosemide, indapamide, and other molecules, not the query.
No query-specific intestinal absorption, permeability, or efflux data; L4/L5 records are for furosemide, metolazone, hydrochlorothiazide, sulpiride, and other molecules.
Transfer from metolazone is structural but not identity; metolazone is a cyclic quinazolinone, while the query is an open salicylanilide.
Possible phenol/amide/sulfonamide conjugation or CYP metabolism is speculative without query-specific evidence.
Species and assay differences (rat microsomes, human liver microsomes, Caco-2) limit quantitative transfer to human oral F.
content.decision_summary: L6 adds only mechanistic hepatic-clearance/metabolic-stability records for other molecules. Related sulfamoyl diuretics show low hepatic extraction (bumetanide C224; azosemide C239/C237), which modestly supports limited first-pass, but no query-specific data exist. The closest structural gold context, metolazone, has high direct F (C25/C42/C61), and all direct gold F values exceed 20% except celecoxib, whose low F is solubility-driven and not transferable. Prediction remains high for F >= 20% with moderate confidence.

You are a senior absolute oral bioavailability F-threshold reasoning model. Integrate evidence direction and transferability without converting uncertainty into a negative outcome. 

L6 adds hepatic-clearance and metabolic-stability experiments. Use them as mechanistic evidence for systemic presystemic loss while preserving species, assay system, and measurement direction; they are not direct oral- bioavailability results or extra gold votes.

This is progressive assay-transfer reasoning. The target is the task endpoint,
not generic permeability, toxicity, or a computational prediction.

Record cards expose source-native values under their original column names.
Missing source values are omitted; do not assume a hidden canonicalized value.


L1 contains the experimental evidence most directly tied to each reference
context's accepted oral-bioavailability outcome. Give greatest endpoint weight
to measured absolute or relative bioavailability and matched oral-versus-
reference exposure; interpret AUC, Cmax, dose, route, formulation, species, and
sampling context together.

L2 adds related experimental records for the same molecule and exact condition.
Use these usually more indirect records to clarify absorption, exposure,
formulation, dose, study design, consistency, limitations, or why an L1 outcome
may not generalize. Permeability, solubility, or mechanism alone is not a direct
oral-bioavailability outcome.


First determine what every measurement says about its reference molecule. L2
records did not define the accepted gold outcome: never count them as extra gold
votes, and do not treat the L1/L2 name itself as a positive or negative label.

Treat transfer_likelihood as one relevance signal for whether a reference
parent-condition context may apply to the query. It is not a positive-class
probability, an experimental result, or a substitute for reasoning about the
visible structure, endpoint, assay, species, formulation, exposure, and
condition. Infer direction from the record cards first, then judge transfer from
all visible context. Do not invent a numeric similarity judgment or assume that
a higher transfer_likelihood must outweigh a concrete experimental mismatch.

Use general medicinal-chemistry knowledge to interpret structures, but ground
every compound-specific empirical claim in the supplied query prior or cited
record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not
independent evidence. Return exactly one valid JSON object and do not reveal
hidden chain-of-thought.
